correctness.rationale: The two zeroth-moment orthogonality equations have determinant u(1-e^{i theta})≠0; solving gives Q(z)=z²-(v/u)(1+e^{i theta})z+v e^{i theta}. Phase rotation yields real monic q(y)=y²-2(v/u)cos(theta/2)y+v with |v|<1; the strict degree-two Schur/Jury test gives the iff condition and exactly one unimodular root at equality. Separated arcs give |cos(theta/2)|<c=cos alpha, while u>=c and v>=2c²-1. If alpha<=acos(1/sqrt3), v>=-1/3 and 1+v>=2|v|, ensuring strictness. Beyond it, symmetric endpoint atoms yield a strict reversed inequality for angles just above 2alpha, and weak approximation by smooth everywhere-positive-on-interior endpoint bumps preserves escape. The endpoint pair phase angle and always-stable uniform density follow from moments and tan t>t. Independently checked 40 finite configurations, not a universal proof.

evidence: Kozhan–Vaktnäs Theorem 5.1 proves unit-disk localization for Laurent MOPUC in an Angelesco setting, not the original type-II polynomial. Gharakhloo et al. advertise a general original-MOPUC reduction but only abstract/partial text was accessible.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The published Laurent result is not a covering theorem. A general determinant reduction might imply the explicit degree-2 coefficient formula, but not necessarily the universal sharp geometric threshold; the uninspected full article remains a risk, not proof of absence.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Even with identical arcs, the Laurent zeros-in-disk theorem cannot be transferred to the original quadratic. Real Schur/Jury conditions are equivalent to its own final zero criterion, but their optimization over all even measures is the proposed new step.

value.rationale: The elementary first nontrivial multi-index is a natural place to decide whether separated arc support forces disk localization, especially given the contrasting Laurent theorem. The sharp all-measure half-width boundary plus smooth full-support failures and uniform-density contrast is a complete structural classification rather than an isolated small-degree numerical example.

final_claim: For original non-Laurent type-II multiple orthogonality at index (1,1) from an even angular probability measure supported on [-alpha,alpha] and its separated rotation, both zeros lie in the open unit disk iff (1+v)u>2|v||cos(theta/2)|, where u=E cos s, v=E cos 2s. Every eligible measure/angle is stable exactly for alpha<=acos(1/sqrt3); above this width smooth positive full-support densities can have an exterior zero, while uniform densities remain stable.
limitations: Only even measures rotated to two strictly separated arcs, alpha<pi/2, original index (1,1).
No higher-degree, nonsymmetric, overlapping-arc or Laurent conclusion.
